steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere and shorter wavelengths of light are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths. Since blue light has a relatively short wavelength, it gets scattered in all directions across the sky, making the entire sky appear blue to an observer on the ground. Longer wavelengths like red and orange pass through more directly, which is why sunsets appear reddish when sunlight travels through a greater thickness of atmosphere.
